blindSummary: In November 2018, the regional order-enforcement agency raided three trans women in this state/province, an incident a comparative foreign-university review of violence against the country's trans women records as police-perpetrated violence. This state/province is also among the eight states/provinces identified in a 2022 study by an international LGBT-rights organisation as having discriminatory regional regulations. No further incidents, arrests, or enacted local bylaws specific to this state/province were found in the dossier period — the evidence base is one documented 2018 raid and membership of the eight-jurisdiction regulatory list, in a belt of states/provinces where order-enforcement campaigns against trans people are consolidating.
blindSourceSummaries: A foreign university's human-rights institute review of violence against trans women in this country: catalogues police-perpetrated violence in 2018, including the November 2018 order-enforcement raid on three trans women in this state/province, against a national backdrop of rising anti-LGBT official rhetoric and non-reporting.

An international LGBT-rights organisation's 2022 study on creeping criminalisation: mapping of national laws and regional regulations that violate the rights of women and LGBTIQ people; identifies discriminatory regional regulations at state/province, district and city level in eight states/provinces — including this one — with significant regional variation in how gender and sexual orientation are penalised locally.
